pattern: 0x00020005|does not support the client's current filePatching setting
meaning: The server refused the -filePatching client because its serverDZ.cfg has no active allowFilePatching = 1; line.
fix: Re-run /dayz-add-server <instance>; it sets allowFilePatching = 1; in .server/<instance>/serverDZ.cfg.

pattern: Mission script has no main function
meaning: The server loaded an empty or broken mission folder, so players can never spawn.
fix: Check that .server/<instance>/mission/init.c defines main(); re-copy it with /dayz-add-server <instance> --refresh-mission.

meaning: A script error earlier in the same log stopped this script module from compiling; nothing in it runs.
fix: Fix the first SCRIPT (E) line with an @"file,line" location above this one; this line is fallout from it.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (script compile errors); dayz-mod-debugger (first error, not the loudest)

meaning: The script names a class the compiler cannot see: a typo, a class from a higher scripts layer (3_Game cannot see 4_World or 5_Mission), or a class from another mod whose CfgPatches is not in requiredAddons.
fix: Check the spelling and the scripts/ layer of the file named on the line. If the class comes from another mod, add that mod's CfgPatches class to requiredAddons and pass the mod to the gate with --deps.
source: dayz-mod-debugger usual causes (Can't find or missing class errors)

meaning: The script refers to a class, variable or function that is not declared where the compiler looks: a typo, a missing declaration, or a missing CfgPatches requiredAddons entry.
fix: Open the file and line named on the error, fix the name or declare it; if it lives in another mod, add that mod to requiredAddons and to --deps.
source: dayz-mod-debugger usual causes (Can't find or missing class errors)

meaning: The script calls a method that does not exist on that class (a typo, or a vanilla API that changed).
fix: Grep P:\scripts\ for the class named on the line and call a method it really has.
source: dayz-lead example (a method that doesn't exist on ItemBase); Tier 2 Vanilla source search

meaning: Script code used an object reference that was null at run time.
fix: Open the first mod file in the stack trace (points_to) and null-check the object before using it (enscript-style.md, null checks).

meaning: A config or material points at a .paa that is not in the loaded data.
fix: Check the path in config.cpp hiddenSelectionsTextures or the .rvmat against the file under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\), and that the .paa exists with a role suffix such as _co.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (missing textures); Tier 2 conventions/assets.md

meaning: A config model= path points at a .p3d that is not in the loaded data.
fix: Check the model= path in config.cpp against the .p3d under workspace/<ModName>/ (paths start at <ModName>\).

meaning: A config lookup failed: the class or property is missing from the loaded config, often a misspelled class or a parent that loads after the mod because CfgPatches requiredAddons does not list it.
fix: Find the class path on the line in workspace/<ModName>/config.cpp; fix the name, add the missing property, or add the parent's CfgPatches class to requiredAddons.
source: dayz-ingame-tester fail rules (missing config classes); dayz-mod-debugger usual causes

meaning: A modded class with an extends clause compiles but is a silent no-op, so the override never runs.
fix: Drop the extends clause: modded class Foo { ... }.

meaning: config.cpp declares no CfgPatches class, so the engine does not load the mod's config.
fix: Add class CfgPatches { class <ModName> { units[] = {}; weapons[] = {}; requiredVersion = 0.1; requiredAddons[] = {}; }; }; to workspace/<ModName>/config.cpp.

meaning: The DayZ Tools work drive is not mounted, so nothing can build or launch.
fix: Mount P: from DayZ Tools (Tools menu, Mount P drive), then gate again.

meaning: AddonBuilder cannot be found.
fix: Install DayZ Tools from Steam, or set DAYZ_TOOLS_PATH to its install root.

pattern: P:\\Mods\\? (?:does not exist|is a regular folder|junction is dangling)
meaning: P:\Mods\ is not a junction to the DayZ !Workshop folder, so built PBOs would not land where the engine loads them.
fix: Recreate the junction: cmd /c mklink /J P:\Mods "<DayZ install>\!Workshop" (remove a regular P:\Mods folder first).

meaning: P:\Mods\@<ModName>\ exists but was not created by this pipeline; it could be a subscribed or hand-placed mod.
fix: If the folder is yours, remove it (cmd /c rmdir /s /q P:\Mods\@<ModName>) and gate again; otherwise rename the mod.

pattern: P:\\\w+ junction is missing|exists as a real folder, not a link
meaning: The P:\<ModName>\ link to workspace/<ModName>/ is missing or wrong, so AddonBuilder cannot read the source.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> --piece junction.

meaning: $PBOPREFIX$ does not hold exactly the mod name, so the PBO's paths would not resolve.
fix: Set workspace/<ModName>/$PBOPREFIX$ to the single line <ModName> and make config.cpp paths start at <ModName>\.

meaning: The mod folder lacks config.cpp or $PBOPREFIX$, which the build needs.
fix: Run /dayz-add-scaffold <ModName> to add the missing file.

meaning: /dayz-launch-test found no PBO for a mod on the launch line.
fix: For the mod under test run /dayz-gate build <ModName>; for a dependency, put its @mod under P:\Mods\ first.
source: docs/dayz-modding.md Troubleshooting (Mod has no built PBO)

meaning: The server instance has no serverDZ.cfg, mission folder or template junction.
fix: Run /dayz-add-server <instance>.

meaning: The DayZ Diag binary that both server and client need is missing.
fix: Verify the DayZ install in Steam, or set DAYZ_DIAG_PATH to DayZDiag_x64.exe.

meaning: Something still holds the server port after the gate stopped DayZDiag.
fix: Close the program holding the port, or run the gate with another --port.

meaning: A bundle PBO ships without its signature; clients that verify signatures reject it.
fix: Put the PBO's .bisign (from the mod's author) next to it in workspace/<ModName>/Addons/ and gate again.
